Course overview

Know what you’re preparing for.

“Merchant Navy” is not one course. It includes officer and rating pathways across deck and engine departments, each with different academic, medical and sea-service requirements. This programme begins with route selection and foundational preparation, then helps students understand recognised training, documentation and the responsibilities of working on commercial vessels.

Who this is for

  • Class 10 students considering a rating pathway such as GP Rating
  • Class 12 PCM students exploring deck or engine officer routes
  • Students comfortable with technical work, routines and time away from home
  • Families who want clarity on eligibility, medical checks and recognised institutions

Career outcomes & reality

Prepare for a pathway—not a promise.

Your next role depends on eligibility, recognised training where required, performance, documents and employer vacancies.

Possible directions

  • Progress toward deck or engine rating roles after recognised training and certification
  • Progress toward deck cadet or marine engineering routes when eligible
  • Long-term officer progression subject to sea service, examinations and certification
  • Port, logistics and shore-based maritime opportunities with additional experience
Indicative industry ranges

What can you earn?

Entry-level trainee/rating compensation can vary broadly, often discussed around ₹20,000–₹60,000 per month while engaged onboard; qualified officer compensation can be substantially higher with rank and experience. These are indicative industry ranges, not guaranteed earnings. Time between contracts may be unpaid, and salaries differ by vessel, employer and certification.

For parents

Make the decision together, with the full picture.

The safest first decision is not a course payment—it is eligibility and medical verification. We ask parents to review the chosen route, the recognised institution responsible for certification, all external costs and the reality that sea jobs depend on vacancies, competence and documents.

Straight answers

Merchant Navy: your questions, answered.

Eligibility, cost, safety and what happens next.

Which Merchant Navy course is best after 12th?

It depends on PCM eligibility, medical fitness, budget and whether you aim for deck, engine or another department. DNS, BSc Nautical Science and marine engineering are distinct routes; verify current DG Shipping and institution criteria.

Can I join after 12th without PCM?

Some rating or hospitality-related maritime routes may be available, but core deck/engine officer pathways generally specify academic subjects. Get a written route assessment before applying.

Is eyesight important for Merchant Navy?

Yes, particularly for deck pathways where colour vision and visual standards matter. Requirements vary and can change; follow current DG Shipping guidelines and obtain the appropriate medical assessment.

Does training guarantee placement on a ship?

No. Training and career guidance do not guarantee onboard employment. Selection, sea-time opportunities and joining depend on eligibility, performance, recruitment and market conditions.
